task.title: Paint shapes
task.shortdesc: A shape has a fill, which paints its inside, and a stroke, which paints its outline. You choose their colors, their opacity, the look of the outline, and gradients, patterns and markers.

step.cmd: Choose the fill and the stroke

info.p: The fill property paints the inside of a shape. Its initial value is black. The stroke property paints the outline, and its initial value is none, so a shape has no outline until you give it a paint. A paint is a color, none, currentColor or a reference to a gradient or a pattern, written as url(#id). After a reference you can write a color that is used when the reference names nothing.

When a shape crosses itself, or has holes, fill-rule decides which areas are inside. With nonzero, the initial value, an inner outline that goes in the same direction as the outer one is filled too, and one that goes in the opposite direction is a hole. With evenodd every second area is empty, whatever the directions are.

The properties fill-opacity and stroke-opacity make each paint transparent, with a number from 0 to 1. The property opacity makes the whole element transparent, fill, stroke and children together, so the overlaps do not show.
These properties change how the outline looks:

ul.li: stroke-width is the thickness. The initial value is 1.
stroke-linecap is the end of an open line: butt ends it flat at the point, round adds a half circle and square adds half the width.
stroke-linejoin is the corner: miter, round or bevel. A sharp miter turns into a bevel when it is longer than stroke-miterlimit times the width, which is 4 initially.

stroke-dasharray makes a dashed line. It is a list of lengths for dashes and gaps, in turn. A list with an odd number of lengths is repeated, so 10 5 3 means 10 5 3 10 5 3. A negative length makes the list invalid.
stroke-dashoffset moves the start of the pattern along the line.

image.alt: Three thick blue lines with butt, round and square ends. Two thick blue angles with a miter and a round corner. Below, three brown lines with long dashes, round dots and a pattern of long and short dashes.

info.p: The paint-order property decides what is painted first. The value stroke paints the outline under the fill, so a thick outline does not cover the inside of the shape. The value fill stroke markers is the initial one.

The pathLength attribute of a shape tells CSSMedia to measure the shape as if it had that length, so lengths in stroke-dasharray scale with it. This line is 80 units long and counts as 100, so each dash of 10 is 8 units long:

stepxmp.pre: <line x1="10" y1="20" x2="90" y2="20" stroke="black" pathLength="100" stroke-dasharray="10 10"/>

info.p: The property vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke keeps the thickness of the outline when a transform scales the shape.

Define a gradient in defs, give it an id and use the reference as a paint. A linearGradient changes the color along a line, and a radialGradient changes it from a center to a circle. The stop elements inside give the colors:

ul.li: offset is the position of the stop, from 0 to 1 or in percent.
stop-color is its color and stop-opacity its opacity.

info.p: A linear gradient goes from x1 y1 to x2 y2, which are 0% 0% and 100% 0% initially, so it goes from left to right. A radial gradient has the center cx cy, the radius r and the focus fx fy, the point where the first stop is painted. These attributes are fractions of the box of the shape. Set gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse" to give them in user units, and use gradientTransform to turn or scale the gradient.

The attribute spreadMethod decides what happens outside the line of the gradient: pad extends the last colors, repeat starts again and reflect goes back. The property color-interpolation set to linearRGB mixes the colors in a linear color space, which gives brighter middle colors.
A gradient can take its stops and attributes from another gradient, named with href. A gradient with one stop paints that color, and a gradient without stops paints nothing.

stepxmp.pre: <defs> <linearGradient id="fade"> <stop offset="0" stop-color="#cfe3f5"/> <stop offset="1" stop-color="#1d4f7a"/> </linearGradient> </defs> <rect width="95" height="70" fill="url(#fade)"/>

info.p: A pattern repeats a small drawing, the tile, to fill a shape. The tile is at x y and has the size width by height. These numbers are fractions of the box of the shape, unless you set patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse". The elements inside the pattern are the drawing of the tile. A viewBox scales it to the tile, and patternTransform turns or scales the whole pattern.

fig.title: A gradient, a radial gradient and a pattern

image.alt: Three rectangles. The first has a linear gradient from light blue on the left to dark blue on the right. The second has a radial gradient from white in the center to dark green at the edges. The third is filled with a regular grid of red dots.

stepxmp.pre: <defs> <pattern id="dots" width="12" height="12" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"> <circle cx="6" cy="6" r="3" fill="#8a2a2a"/> </pattern> </defs> <rect width="95" height="70" fill="url(#dots)"/>

info.p: A marker is a small drawing that CSSMedia repeats on the vertices of a line, a polyline, a polygon or a path. Define it in defs and name it in these properties of the shape: marker-start for the first vertex, marker-mid for the ones between and marker-end for the last. The property marker sets the three at once.
These attributes of the marker element control the mark:

ul.li: markerWidth and markerHeight give its size, 3 by 3 initially. A viewBox scales the drawing to that size.
refX and refY give the point of the mark that goes on the vertex.
orient is the direction. With auto the mark follows the direction of the line, and with an angle it is fixed.
markerUnits is strokeWidth initially, so the mark is scaled by the thickness of the line. With userSpaceOnUse it has the size of its numbers.

image.alt: A zigzag line with red dots at its start and at its two inner corners, and a blue arrow at its end. Next to it, a curve ends with an arrow that points along the curve.

stepxmp.pre: <defs> <marker id="arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" markerWidth="5" markerHeight="5" refX="5" refY="5" orient="auto"> <path d="M0 0 L10 5 L0 10 Z" fill="#1d4f7a"/> </marker> </defs> <path d="M230 80 Q 260 10 300 60" fill="none" stroke="#555555" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
